chunks: And by his chain, from Yunus, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) has performed Hajj and 'Umrah.
I asked, "Does it replace Hajjat al-Islam (the obligatory pilgrimage) for him?"
He said, "No, it is the Hajj for the weak (one who cannot afford or travel) until he becomes strong (able), and then he must perform Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah."
"Do you not know that seventy thousand angels circulate the House (Ka'bah) every day? Until night overtakes them, they ascend and others descend, and they circulate the House until morning."
"And indeed, Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is more honorable to Allah than the House."
"And indeed, at the time of each prayer, seventy thousand disheveled and dust-covered angels descend to him, and they will not have another turn (to return) until the Day of Judgment."

key_terms.الْبَيْتُ: Al-Bayt (The House, referring to the Ka'bah)
key_terms.شُعْثٌ غُبْرٌ: Shu'thun ghur (disheveled and dust-covered, describing angels)

ai.seo_question: Does visiting Imam Husayn's grave replace the obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (a.s.) clarifies that Ziyarah to Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.) serves as a valid substitute for the obligatory Hajj only for those unable to travel to the Ka'bah due to weakness or lack of means; once capable, one must still perform the actual Hajj. This distinction highlights the superior spiritual status of the Imam, as seventy thousand angels descend to his grave at every prayer time, a honor surpassing the constant circulation of angels around the Ka'bah.
